history.summary: Vaishnavite temple at the Tunga-Bhadra sangama at Koodli (also spelled Kudli/Kudali), the village itself (CSV town 'Shimoga' corrected: Shimoga is the district headquarters; the temple is at Koodli, ~16-18 km from Shivamogga). Puranic tradition holds Vishnu gave darshan to Prahlada here as Chintamani Narasimha, and the idol - seated in veerasana holding a small bowl - is believed to have been consecrated by Prahlada. The east-facing temple is dated 'perhaps 12th century or later'; it has a closed sabha mandapa, sukanasi and garbha-griha on a Hoysala plan with a three-tiered Rajagopuram in Keladi style adorned with the Hoysala royal crest. It stands beside the 8th-century Sangameshwara and the 12th-century Rameshwara temples in Koodli's ancient cluster (sometimes called the Dakshina Kashi or Varanasi of the South). Koodli is also a noted matha centre: the Koodli Shankaracharya mutt (Sringeri branch) and the Koodli Arya Akshobhya Tirtha Matha (Dvaita). Do not confuse with Kudalasangama, ~300 km north at the Malaprabha-Krishna confluence. Coordinates are the village centre (temple lies within the village); no documented darshan timings or specific festival list found - verify locally.

name: Sri Chintamani Narasimha Temple
town_description: Koodli (Kudli/Kudali) is a historic village in Shivamogga district, about 16-18 km from Shivamogga city, at the confluence (sangama) of the Tunga and Bhadra rivers which form the Tungabhadra. A pilgrimage centre since Mahabharata-era legend, it hosts a cluster of ancient temples and two historic mathas, and is called the Dakshina Kashi or Varanasi of the South.

travel.road: ~16-18 km from Shivamogga via Holehonnur (3 km away)
